tob-14500-d1: Grimms’ Fairy Tales — the Kinder- und Hausmärchen — gathers the brothers’ immortal folk tales: Cinderella, Snow White, Hansel and Gretel, Rapunzel, and more. The 1812 collection founded folklore studies. Every child knows these tales. The book remains the world’s best-loved storybook.
tob-14502-d1: The Persian Mystics: Jalalu’d-din Rumi introduces the great Sufi poet of Konya — the whirling dervishes’ master. The Masnavi author’s life, teachings, and verses are presented. His couplets have guided seekers for centuries. The book is a gateway to Rumi’s timeless wisdom.
tob-14503-d1: Cheragh Ali’s book on the popular ‘Jihad’ — 1885 — pleads for a mild reading of jihad in the Qur’an and the old lore. The Indian Muslim scholar’s pages met the war-cries of his day. His pen-work broke new ground. The book is a landmark of new Islam thought.
tob-14505-d1: Conservation of marine birds of northern North America — edited by James C. Bartonek — addresses the protection of northern seabirds. The technical volume belongs to wildlife conservation science. Its data guide policy. The book is a specialist’s resource on marine birds.
tob-14506-d1: A. A. Milne’s When We Were Very Young — 1924 — gathers the beloved verses of childhood, with E. H. Shepard’s illustrations. Christopher Robin’s poems charmed generations of children. Half the rhymes are known by heart. The book is a classic of children’s verse.
tob-4004-d1: Walt Whitman’s Drum-Taps — 1865 — gathers his Civil War poems, from the drums of muster to Lincoln’s death. The good gray poet sang the war’s suffering and glory. O Captain! My Captain! is here. The collection is the great poetic record of the war.
tob-4006-d1: Richard Carlile’s Church Reform: The Only Means to That End — an open letter to Sir Robert Peel — demands disestablishment of the Church of England. The radical publisher’s pamphlet attacked church privilege. The work is a relic of reform agitation.
tob-4008-d1: Worthington Hooker’s Science for the School and Family, Part I: Natural Philosophy introduces physics to young readers at home and school. The physician-educator’s clear textbook served nineteenth-century schools. Its lessons shaped young minds. The book is a relic of early science education.
tob-4148-d1: E. H. Palmer’s translation of the Qur’an, Part II — Sacred Books of the East, Vol. IX — gives the latter half of Islam’s scripture in English. The Cambridge orientalist’s version served Victorian readers. The volume opened the Qur’an to the English world.
tob-4151-d1: Henry A. Homes’s book on the great Muslim thinker al-Ghazali — done from the Turkish — limns the sage of Islam. His thought ruled Moslem god-lore for ages. The book bore the sage to English readers. His Incoherence met the thinkers head-on.
tob-4170-d1: Thomas Bulfinch’s Mythology — the omnibus of Age of Fable, Age of Chivalry, and Legends of Charlemagne — retells the world’s great myths and legends. The Boston banker’s book taught America its classics. The volume remains the beloved popular mythology.
tob-4185-d1: Plutarch’s Lives, Vol. I — in John and William Langhorne’s translation — covers the Greek lives from Theseus to Pericles. The biographer’s parallel lives shaped the Western imagination. Shakespeare mined it for his Romans. The volume is the classic of ancient biography.
tob-4189-d1: Frederic Pincott’s Hitopadesa — a new literal translation from the Sanskrit text — gives the classic Indian book of fables. The witty animal tales teach statecraft and worldly wisdom. Kings learned policy from its pages. The book is the Sanskrit Aesop.
tob-4196-d1: Rudolf Steiner’s Story of My Life — in the authorized translation — is the autobiography of the great Austrian anthroposophist. The founder of Waldorf education tells his spiritual journey. His path led from Goethe to the spirit. The book is essential for students of Steiner.
tob-4203-d1: Bessie Rebecca Burchett’s Janus in Roman Life and Cult — a study in Roman religions — examines the two-faced god in Roman public and private life. The scholarly monograph illuminates Roman ritual. The book is a specialist’s work on Roman religion.
tob-4218-d1: Rufus M. Jones’s Studies in Mystical Religion — 1909 — explores the great mystics of the Christian tradition. The Quaker scholar’s work is the classic American study of mysticism. His sympathy illuminates every page. The book remains essential for students of the subject.
tob-4272-d1: James Legge’s She-King — the Book of Poetry — Vol. IV, Part I of the Chinese Classics — gives the ancient Chinese songs in English. The missionary-sinologist’s version is the classic translation. The book opened Chinese poetry to the West.
tob-4274-d1: The Popol Vuh — in Abbé Brasseur de Bourbourg’s edition with French translation — is the sacred book of the Quiché Maya. The creation epic is the great text of Maya literature. The book is the cornerstone of pre-Columbian letters.
tob-4284-d1: E. A. Wallis Budge’s Vocabulary in Hieroglyphic to the Theban Recension of the Book of the Dead is the great Egyptologist’s hieroglyphic word-list. The reference work serves students of hieroglyphs. Its pages unlock the dead. The book is a specialist’s tool.
tob-4291-d1: James George Frazer’s Golden Bough — second edition, Vol. II — continues the great comparative study of magic and religion. The Cambridge scholar’s vast work reshaped anthropology. The dying god is its theme. Its influence endures today. The volume is part of the monumental classic.
tob-4293-d1: R. A. Nicholson’s translation of Jalaluddin Rumi’s Mathnawi — Vol. II — gives the great Persian Sufi epic in English. The Cambridge scholar’s version is the classic English rendering. Its tales teach the mystic path. The volume continues the six-book masterpiece.
tob-9047-d1: Luigi Barzini’s Al fronte — At the Front, May to October 1915 — reports from the Italian front of the Great War. The famous journalist’s dispatches capture the war’s first months. His prose brings the trenches alive. The book is a classic of war reportage.
tob-9052-d1: Hermitte and Bodenbender’s Buenos Aires stone-book — the teaching list of the rock hoard — names each stone in the town’s keeping. The Spanish book served Argentine rock-men. Its notes limn each stone. The book stays a time-mark of the old museum.
tob-9063-d1: E. Lee Ryan’s Five Little Bush Girls — illustrated by Betty Paterson — is an Australian children’s book of outback adventures. The bush girls’ escapades charmed young readers. Its pictures capture the bush. The book is a relic of Australian children’s literature.
tob-9119-d1: Romesh C. Dutt’s Ramayana and Mahabharata Condensed into English Verse retells India’s two great epics in verse. The Bengali scholar’s rendering brought the epics to English readers. Rama’s exile and the Kurus’ war unfold. The book is a classic of Indian literature in translation.
tob-9287-d1: Charles F. Aiken’s Laws of Manu — a Catholic Encyclopedia article — surveys the ancient Hindu law code. The concise entry introduces Manu’s ordinances on duty and society. Its judgments are fair and learned. The article is a useful reference on Hindu law.
tob-9385-d1: Robertson’s foreword to Athanasius’s four great anti-Arian talks limns the 300s Godhead row. The Oxford man’s pages light the old fight. Arius denied the Son’s full Godhead. The Nicene faith hung in the wind. His reading stays worth its hire. The book serves God-lore students.
